issues.issue: The ERISA regime is triggered only if Lender notifies Borrower that Plan assets are involved, and the section does not say what happens to a Loan in fact funded with Plan assets where no notice was given.

The consequence of Lender's failure to 'communicate and keep current' the fiduciary information is that Lender 'shall be deemed to have made' Borrower's representation, a deeming whose scope and effect on the Loan is not spelled out.
The daily mark-to-market duty is imposed 'pursuant to Section 9.7', but the Agreement's Section 9 ends at 9.6, so the operative mechanic is cited to a provision that does not exist.

Delivery is due within 'the lesser of' three periods including 'the time negotiated for such delivery', yet the proviso allows the parties to agree a longer period, so a negotiated longer period is both included in and excluded from the 'lesser of' test.

This makes Collateral security 'only' for Borrower's obligations to the Plan, whereas Section 4.2 makes Collateral security for 'any other obligations of Borrower to Lender hereunder' and Section 18 allows set-off across all Loans.

The single-agreement, cross-default and cross-Loan set-off treatment is difficult to reconcile with Annex I-A section 4, which treats the portion of each Loan allocable to each Principal as a separate Loan, and with Section 17.4(d)'s Plan-only collateral limit.

Section 21 makes all obligations with respect to any Loan survive termination of the Agreement, while Section 24.1 permits termination on notice 'subject only to fulfillment of any obligations then outstanding', leaving the post-termination position stated two different ways.

A notice is 'deemed effective' when 'delivery was in good faith attempted' even if never received, and 'good faith attempted' is given no content; the telephone proviso adds a further undefined precondition.

The integration clause is opened by 'Except as otherwise agreed by the parties' and is limited to agreements 'concerning loans of Securities', so which prior or collateral arrangements survive is left genuinely open.

Termination on notice is 'subject only to fulfillment of any obligations then outstanding', which does not say whether termination is deferred until outstanding Loans are closed or is immediate with obligations surviving.

The no-oral-modification rule cannot easily be squared with Section 24.2, which expressly allows agreements under Sections 10.5(b) and 25.37 to be made orally, and with the definitions of Close of Business and Cutoff Time that permit agreement 'orally or in writing'.
'Time is of the essence' sits uneasily with Sections 12.4 and 12.8, which make a failure a Default only after notice and a cure period running to the next day's Cutoff Time.
Section 24.2 permits agreements to be made orally if promptly confirmed, which pulls against the same Section 24.1 requirement that the Agreement be modified only by a signed writing.

The definition ends its enumerated insolvency laws with the catch-all 'or similar law', leaving the reach of that phrase (for example to regulatory or receivership regimes) to be fixed by construction.

The definition sweeps in any such person 'regardless of whether the activities of such person are conducted in the United States or otherwise require such person to register', which makes the class broader than the enumerated registered categories suggest and controls Lender's Retransfer and segregation duties under Section 4.2.

'Business Day' is given three different meanings in one definition (by reference to the Loaned Securities' market, to the market of the security being valued, and a special Section 9 meaning), so which applies to any given deadline is not always plain.
The definition cross-refers to 'Section 3.1', but 'Cash Collateral Fee' is defined in Section 5.1; Section 3.1 concerns transfer of Loaned Securities and contains no such definition.

Failing agreement, 'Close of Business' is whatever is 'determined in accordance with market practice', an unspecified external standard that fixes the deadline for collateral and payment obligations throughout the Agreement.

The definition's residual limb for a Customer Lender extends to 'any other property permitted to serve as collateral ... pursuant to exemptive, interpretive or no-action relief or otherwise', a catch-all whose boundary against the enumerated cash, Treasuries and letters of credit is indeterminate.

Whether a Lender is a 'Customer' turns on being a customer of Borrower 'under Rule 15c3-3 ... (to the extent that Borrower is subject to such Rule)', and that status switches on Sections 9.1, 4.2 and the Collateral definition without any test the parties can apply on their own.
Absent agreement the 'Cutoff Time' is left to 'market practice', an undefined external benchmark although it governs when transfers under Sections 3, 4, 6 and 12 become late.

'Distribution' is defined by an open list headed 'including, but not limited to', beginning with the wholly general 'cash and all other property', so the reach of the enumerated categories against that general limb is uncertain.
